newsitem.title: UK: UK warns of European conflict if NATO doesn't grow.
newsitem.headline: UK warns of European conflict if NATO doesn't grow.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind warned on Monday that Europe could be plunged into fresh ethnic and nationalistic conflict if Russia succeeded in blocking NATO's plans for expansion.
In a speech Rifkind was to give to the Carnegie Endowment

for International Peace in Washington on Monday and released in advance in London, he said that unless the 16-nation alliance accepted new members, former Soviet allies in eastern Europe would be cut off by a new Iron Curtain descending over the continent.

"They would have to make their own security arrangements, independent of the countries to their west whose interests and values they share...Local and regional alliances would spring up in a frightening facsimile of pre-Second World War Europe," he said.
"There could be new tremors along ethnic and nationalistic faultlines. A dismal prospect indeed and one that could easily draw us in Western Europe and America into new tension and conflict."

Moscow has long opposed NATO's enlargement plans on the grounds that they endanger Russia's security, but the alliance insists it will go ahead with a July summit in Madrid at which it intends to invite at least three former Warsaw Pact states to start talks on membership.
